hypothesis: If Arizona climate fluctuated with a regular period of almost exactly 150 years, century-smoothed Arizona pine ring-width chronologies spanning the last 500 years show a significant spectral peak at about 150 years.
pass_criterion: In multitaper or maximum-entropy spectra of Arizona ponderosa pine ring-width chronologies covering 1500–1900 CE, a peak between 140 and 160 years is significant at 95% against a red-noise null, in at least two independent chronologies.
fail_criterion: No spectral peak between 140 and 160 years is significant at 95% in any chronology, or the strongest significant peak lies outside 120–180 years.
interpretation: 'Yellow pine' is read as ponderosa pine (Pinus ponderosa). 'Century-smoothed' becomes a 100-year smoother or detrending of standardized ring widths. 'Regular periodicity' is read as a statistically significant narrow spectral peak. The record is only about three cycles long, so low-frequency power is poorly resolved.

dataset.name: International Tree-Ring Data Bank (ITRDB)
dataset.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, World Data Service for Paleoclimatology
dataset.why_it_fits: ITRDB has downloadable ring-width measurement and chronology files by site and species, including Arizona Pinus ponderosa sites. The fields used are year and standardized ring-width index.
